subject: physics

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Accuracy
lines: Accuracy is how close a measured value is
to the true value of the quantity.
It depends on how far the errors have
steps.why: Accuracy is measured against the TRUE value, so it needs an outside standard. A reading can be repeatable and still be far from the truth.
common_mistakes: Saying accuracy is how close the readings are to each other. That is precision.

recall.must_convey: That accuracy is the closeness of a measured value to the true value.

steps.memory_tip: Accuracy points OUTWARD to the true value. Precision points INWARD at the readings themselves.
steps.margin_note: One line each. The examiner is looking for the pair, not an essay.

steps.label: Precision

lines.text: Precision: how close the readings are to each other

lines: It depends on the least count of the
instrument, not on the true value.
steps.why: Precision is set by the instrument. A finer least count gives readings that cluster tightly, whether or not that cluster sits on the true value.
common_mistakes: Writing that a precise measurement must be accurate. A zero error gives tight readings that are all wrong.

recall.must_convey: That precision is the closeness among several measured values, and depends on the least count.

steps.memory_tip: Precision comes from the instrument — say "least count" and the second mark is earned.
steps.margin_note: Name the least count here. It is the word that separates the two ideas.

insider_note: Both books ask this one. Two marks means two contrasts — write accuracy and precision as a pair, never one alone.
